items.question: Why do scriptural injunctions to undertake initiation constitute valid authority?
premises: Scriptures prescribe undertaking initiation.
Such scriptures are cited as beginning with injunctions like undertaking initiation.
Revealed scriptures function as valid authority.
items.inference: Therefore, scriptural statements enjoining initiation are authoritative.
items.plain_english: O beloved, scriptures that say one should undertake initiation and so forth are valid authority.

items.question: What further teaching does the goddess of Kula wish to hear briefly?
premises: The speaker addresses the goddess of Kula.
The exposition has been given in brief.
The listener may desire to hear more.
items.inference: The speaker asks what more the listener wishes to hear.
items.plain_english: O goddess of Kula, what more do you wish to hear in brief?

items.question: Which chapter bears the title narration of the greatness of Kula?
premises: A narration of the greatness of Kula is named.
The named section is identified as a chapter.
That chapter is the second one.
items.inference: The second chapter is titled the narration of the greatness of Kula.
items.plain_english: This is the second chapter, named the narration of the greatness of Kula.

items.question: What request is made to the lord regarding the upper tradition and its mantra?
premises: The upper tradition is an object of inquiry.
Its mantra and greatness are also sought.
The lord is asked to explain them.
items.inference: The listener requests the lord to tell of the upper tradition, its mantra, and its greatness.
items.plain_english: O lord, tell me about the upper tradition, its mantra, and its greatness.

items.question: What effect does merely hearing that teaching have upon the deity?
premises: The teaching can be heard.
Mere hearing is sufficient contact with it.
The deity responds favorably to that hearing.
items.inference: By merely hearing it, the deity becomes well pleased.
items.plain_english: By merely hearing it, the deity becomes well pleased.

items.question: Why does the speaker agree to reveal the upper tradition to the beloved?
premises: The speaker promises to tell the upper tradition.
Affection motivates the disclosure.
The listener is urged to listen.
items.inference: Out of affection, the speaker will reveal the upper tradition to the beloved.
items.plain_english: Out of affection I will tell you of the upper tradition; listen, O beloved.

items.question: How are all Shaiva and Shakta scriptures characterized in this teaching?
premises: Shaiva and Shakta scriptures form a recognized class.
All members of this class are considered together.
They are declared to be secret.
items.inference: All Shaiva and Shakta scriptures are declared secret.
uncertainties: The exact form parikīttītāḥ may reflect a textual variant of parikīrtitāḥ.
items.plain_english: All the Shaiva and Shakta scriptures are declared to be secret.

items.question: What degree of secrecy is attributed to this teaching addressed to the Mother?
premises: There exist secrets beyond ordinary secrets.
This teaching is compared to them.
It is identified as their secret.
items.inference: This teaching is the secret of secrets.
items.plain_english: O Mother, this is the secret of secrets.

items.question: What change occurs now regarding the teaching previously concealed with effort?
premises: The teaching was well concealed by the speaker.
The concealment was maintained with effort.
Now a contrasting action takes place.
items.inference: The teaching that was carefully concealed is now being revealed.
items.plain_english: I carefully kept it well concealed, but now it is being revealed.

items.question: How many paths to liberation are declared together with the upper tradition?
premises: The upper tradition is included in a set.
The set is counted as five.
These are declared paths to liberation.
items.inference: The upper tradition and these others are declared as five paths to liberation.
uncertainties: The exact form prakīttītāḥ may reflect a textual variant of prakīrtitāḥ.
items.plain_english: The upper tradition and these others are declared to be five paths to liberation.

items.question: What attitude toward deliberation is enjoined regarding this declared truth?
premises: The statement is affirmed as truth.
The listener is directly addressed.
Deliberation in this matter is negated.
items.inference: This is true, and no deliberation should be made about it here.
items.plain_english: This is true, O fair-hipped one; no deliberation should be made about it here.

items.question: Where were those paths previously declared to the lady of Kula?
premises: Certain paths were mentioned earlier.
This tantra is the locus of teaching.
The declaration was made previously in it.
items.inference: Those paths were previously declared in this tantra.
items.plain_english: O lady of Kula, they were previously declared in this tantra.
